correctness.rationale: For every even n>=4, at most two spokes occur. The one-spoke layer collapses to the full boundary simplex on the n clockwise rim arcs. Every pair of spokes has an explicit link: adjacent pairs have a sphere link and yield an (n-1)-ball attached along S^(n-2), while all other pairs have conical links whose blocks are homotopy-trivial relative to the base. Sending all spokes to odd rim arc e_1 supplies a simplicial retraction to the rim sphere; since this map extends over each special block and is an equivalence on the one-spoke layer, every high-cell attaching map is null. Exactly n/2 special pairs therefore yield S^(n-2) wedge n/2 copies of S^(n-1). A standalone checker exhaustively rederived all faces, links and mod-two boundaries for n=4,6,8,10. No finite observation is used as a proof for arbitrary n.

value.rationale: This is a genuinely all-parameter integral homotopy classification of a canonical, strongly connected oriented wheel family, rather than a small-case computation or an arbitrary vertex slice. It yields mixed adjacent-dimensional homology of rank 1 and unbounded rank m, with an explicit geometric explanation in terms of adjacent spoke pairs and a genuine simplicial retraction. It provides a new connected-family realization pattern for multipath complexes in the context of published questions about mixed-dimensional sphere wedges. It neither solves a general realization problem nor asserts such a downstream consequence.
